text: An end-to-end cafe platform where ordering happens through an AI chat agent built on Google Gemini. The conversation layer is served by a FastAPI backend that talks to Cloud SQL for state, and the whole thing runs as a Cloud Run service — a real, publicly reachable deployment rather than a localhost demo. The live URL above is the actual production service: send a message, and the agent interprets the order, grounds it in menu data, and handles the back-and-forth.

A complete ML engineering exercise: from raw customer data to a deployed scoring API. Model optimization covers threshold tuning (rather than defaulting to 0.5) and balanced training with SMOTE, and the trained artifact sits behind a FastAPI endpoint that consumes feature vectors and returns predictions.

Grounded question-answering over financial documents: PDF upload, page-level extraction with PyMuPDF, section-aware overlapping chunks, BGE embeddings into persistent ChromaDB, and answer generation behind REST APIs (FastAPI + Streamlit UI, Docker Compose). Every answer ships with file/page/section citations and similarity scores — and when no relevant chunk is retrieved, the system returns an insufficient-context response instead of calling the LLM. Evaluation is built in: RAGAS metrics, NDCG@k, deterministic sentence-level hallucination detection, and a benchmark runner that flags faithfulness regressions, exposed through a FastAPI /evaluate endpoint.

Fine-tuned Llama 3.2 3B Instruct with QLoRA on 150 SQL-to-explanation examples covering CTEs, window functions, and JOINs — trained in under 1 GPU-hour on a Kaggle T4 and exported to a ~2 GB Q4_K_M GGUF model, published at huggingface.co/ShindeGaurav-207/SQL2NL and served through FastAPI with llama.cpp/Ollama. Quality is measured, not asserted: a keyword-coverage, MiniLM semantic-similarity, and latency harness scores held-out queries — 6/8 passed with 0.74 average semantic similarity and 65.1% keyword coverage. pytest tests and GitHub Actions CI keep the pipeline reproducible end to end.

A LangGraph agent turns natural language into SQL: intent parsing, example retrieval, SQL generation, execution, validation, and up to 3 bounded self-correction retries, exposed through both a CLI and a FastAPI endpoint. Security is first-class: read-only SQL execution behind a SELECT/WITH-only statement gate, a read-only database connection, a LIMIT guard, and a query timeout — with a STRIDE threat model covering cache poisoning. The evaluation is leakage-controlled on 28 held-out Chinook questions: baseline 60.7%, retry-only 57.1%, retry plus correction memory 57.1% execution accuracy. Correction memory gave no measurable gain (overlapping 95% CIs) and nested queries were weakest at 28.6% — both honest results reported, not hidden. 150 offline tests back the pipeline.

AI Engineer at TCS building Generative AI, RAG, LLM fine-tuning, and AI-agent systems with open-source LLMs (Llama), LangChain/LangGraph, vector databases, and FastAPI. Also ships in-browser AI: this portfolio runs a real language model in the visitor's browser — no server, no API keys.

AI agents (LangChain, LangGraph, tool calling, self-correction loops, text-to-SQL).
